Triage notes (first pass):
- Telemetry shows rapid growth in request queue length on runtime-pool-07 (dedicated) beginning 07:47. CPU/GPU utilization is high and KV-cache miss rate spiked ~07:50.
- Error traces show most 5xx are internal timeouts in the runtime layer (worker process busy / queue timeout), not a downstream integration.
- One suspicious signal: we saw a pattern of large, untrimmed batched requests from Lodestar (longer sequence lengths) which amplify KV cache pressure.

Mitigation recommended (immediate):
1) Enable emergency auto-scale for pool-07 (add 2 GPUs) — ETA 6–8 minutes.
2) Route Lodestar traffic to fallback model-quantized-v2 (lower memory footprint; slightly higher latency per token but much lower tail).
3) Apply short-term per-API throttling on max-concurrent requests for Lodestar to smooth bursts.

I'm standing up a war‑room at 09:00 PDT to coordinate infra + infra‑ops + account. Attendees: Monica (triage), Karthik (runtime), Laura (customer comms), Marissa (exec liaison), Alex (AM).

What happened (short):
- Starting ~07:47 PDT a subset of large batched requests triggered KV cache pressure on the dedicated runtime pool serving Lodestar, increasing queue length and leading to internal timeouts. This manifested as higher p90/p95 latency and a 5–6% 5xx spike.

Actions we took (completed):

- Traffic routing: we moved Lodestar to model-quantized-v2 at 08:55 as a fallback to reduce memory pressure.
- Protective throttling applied to max-concurrent for Lodestar to smooth bursts.
- We ran curated regressions against your sample trace; errors decreased and p95 is trending down.

- Root cause postmortem in development (target EOD).
- We'll provide a sequence-length advisory and suggested batching limits to avoid cache thrash.
